column1: Articles|Choose the article: She is ___ honest person.|an|a|the only|no article always|Honest begins with a vowel sound because its initial h is silent, so an is appropriate here.
Articles|Choose the article: He works at ___ university.|a|an|any article is impossible|these|University begins with a consonant /y/ sound, so a is used before it in this indefinite reference.
Articles|Choose the article: We waited for ___ hour.|an|a|those|many|Hour begins with a vowel sound because h is silent; article choice depends on sound.
Agreement|Complete the sentence: Each of the books ___ a label.|has|have|are|were|The head subject each is singular; the plural phrase of the books does not control the verb.
Agreement|Complete the sentence: Neither of the two answers ___ correct.|is|are being always|have|were being always|In this formal construction neither of the two takes a singular verb.
Agreement|Complete the sentence: The list of items ___ on the desk.|is|are|have|do|The subject is list, not items, so the present verb is singular.
Agreement|Complete the sentence: My brother and I ___ ready.|are|is|am|has|Two subjects joined by and normally take a plural verb; brother and I is plural.
Agreement|Complete the sentence: Mathematics ___ my favourite subject.|is|are|have|do|The name of the subject mathematics is singular in this use despite its final s.
Tenses|Complete the sentence: She ___ here since 2020.|has lived|lived yesterday|is live|have lived|Has lived connects a situation beginning in the past with the present; she takes has.
Tenses|Complete the sentence: By the time we arrived, the train ___.|had left|will leaving|has leave|leaving|The past perfect marks the earlier of two past events: the train left before the arrival.
Tenses|Complete the sentence: Look! The children ___ in the park.|are playing|plays|has played|is playing|The present continuous describes an activity in progress, with plural children taking are.

Tenses|Complete the sentence: If it rains tomorrow, we ___ indoors.|will stay|stayed|had stayed|has stayed|A common first conditional uses present tense in the if clause and will in the result clause.
Tenses|Complete the sentence: If I were taller, I ___ reach that shelf.|could|have|am|did|This hypothetical present condition uses were and a modal such as could in the result clause.
Prepositions|Complete the sentence: She is interested ___ astronomy.|in|at|on|for|The adjective interested commonly takes the preposition in before its subject matter.
Prepositions|Complete the sentence: He is responsible ___ maintaining the records.|for|of|to only|in only|Responsible for expresses a duty or task assigned to someone.
Prepositions|Complete the sentence: The keys are ___ the table.|on|from|during|until|On describes contact with the table's upper surface in this sentence.
Prepositions|Complete the sentence: We arrived ___ the station at noon.|at|on|for|by only|At is normally used for arrival at a specific place such as a station.

Prepositions|Complete the sentence: The gift was divided equally ___ the two children.|between|during|since|beneath|Between is appropriate for the stated pair. Distinguish spatial and time prepositions.
Pronouns|Complete the sentence: This is the student ___ won the prize.|who|which|where|when|Who introduces a relative clause referring to a person as its subject.
Pronouns|Complete the sentence: The book ___ you lent me is useful.|that|where|when|whose name|That can introduce a restrictive relative clause referring to the book.
Pronouns|Choose the correct form: Please give the receipt to ___.|me|I|mine|myself alone|After the preposition to, the object pronoun me is appropriate.
Pronouns|Complete the sentence: She completed the work by ___.|herself|her ownself|hisself|theirself|Herself is the standard reflexive form corresponding to she.

Voice|Choose the correct passive: The clerk checked the form.|The form was checked by the clerk.|The form checked the clerk.|The form is checking by the clerk.|The clerk was checked by the form.|The object becomes the passive subject; simple past checked becomes was checked.

Voice|Choose the correct passive: They will announce the result.|The result will be announced.|The result will announced.|The result is announce.|The result has announce.|A future passive uses will be followed by the past participle.

Voice|Choose the correct passive: Someone has repaired the bridge.|The bridge has been repaired.|The bridge has repairing.|The bridge have repair.|The bridge repaired someone.|The present perfect passive is has or have been plus the past participle.

Narration|Choose the reported form with normal past reporting: He said, "I am tired."|He said that he was tired.|He said that I am tired.|He said that he tired.|He said that he were tired.|The speaker's I becomes he, and am commonly shifts to was with past reporting in this context.

Narration|Choose the reported question: She asked me, "Where do you live?"|She asked me where I lived.|She asked me where did I live.|She asked me where do I lived.|She asked me where I living.|An indirect question uses statement word order; the pronoun and tense adjust to the reporting context.

Narration|Choose the reported command: The teacher said to us, "Open your books."|The teacher told us to open our books.|The teacher said us open your books.|The teacher told that we opening books.|The teacher asked where our books open.|A reported command commonly uses told plus object plus to-infinitive, with the possessive adjusted.

Conjunctions|Complete the sentence: ___ it was raining, we continued walking.|Although|Because of|Despite of|During|Although introduces a clause and expresses contrast. Despite normally takes a noun or gerund, not of.
Conjunctions|Complete the sentence: Work carefully ___ you make a mistake.|or|because of|during|despite of|Or can introduce an undesirable alternative consequence in this sentence.
Conjunctions|Complete the sentence: Both Rina ___ Meera attended.|and|or|nor|but also only|Both pairs with and; either pairs with or, and neither pairs with nor.
Conjunctions|Complete the sentence: Neither the red pen ___ the blue pen works.|nor|and|but|so|Neither pairs with nor to connect the two alternatives.
Modifiers|Choose the correct form: She writes ___.|neatly|neat|neater person|neatness|An adverb modifies the verb writes; neatly states how she writes.
Modifiers|Choose the correct form: This solution is ___ than the first.|simpler|most simple of all|simple only|simplest of two|Than introduces a comparison; simpler is the comparative form used here.
Modifiers|Choose the correct form: Of the three routes, this is the ___.|shortest|shorter|short|shortly|A comparison across the three routes calls for the superlative shortest.

Modifiers|Choose the corrected sentence.|She is too tired to continue.|She is too tired that continue.|She is too tired for continue.|She is too tired to continuing.|Too plus adjective plus to-infinitive expresses excessive degree preventing the action.
Vocabulary|Choose a synonym of concise.|Brief|Lengthy|Uncertain|Noisy|Concise means expressing information briefly and clearly.
Vocabulary|Choose an antonym of scarce.|Abundant|Rare|Limited|Insufficient|Scarce means in short supply; abundant indicates a plentiful supply.

Vocabulary|Choose the word for a person who studies stars and other celestial objects.|Astronomer|Astrologer|Geologist|Botanist|Astronomy scientifically studies celestial objects; astrology is a different practice.
Vocabulary|Choose the word for a person who compiles a dictionary.|Lexicographer|Cartographer|Calligrapher|Biographer|Lexicography concerns compiling dictionaries; cartography concerns maps.

Idioms|What does "once in a blue moon" mean?|Very rarely|Every morning|Without warning every time|At exactly midnight|This idiom describes something that happens infrequently, not a literal moon schedule.

Idioms|What does "a piece of cake" mean in an informal description of a task?|Something easy|Something impossible|Something secret|Something expensive|The idiom means the task is easy; interpret expressions in context rather than literally.

Idioms|What does "break the ice" mean in a social setting?|Ease initial tension and start interaction|End every friendship|Cancel a meeting permanently|Freeze a drink|The idiom refers to helping people become comfortable enough to interact.

Editing|Choose the correctly spelled verb meaning to provide space or lodging.|Accommodate|Acommodate|Accomodate|Acomodate|Accommodate has double c and double m; check common spelling patterns carefully.
Editing|Choose the correctly spelled word meaning to keep apart.|Separate|Seperate|Separete|Seperete|Separate is spelled with a after the first r; pronunciation can make this word misleading.

Editing|Choose the corrected sentence expressing a preference between tea and coffee.|I prefer tea to coffee.|I prefer tea than coffee.|I prefer tea over than coffee.|I prefers tea to coffee.|In the prefer X to Y construction, to introduces the comparison and I takes prefer.

Editing|Choose the corrected sentence reporting a suggestion to go early.|She suggested going early.|She suggested to go early.|She suggested me go early.|She suggested going to early.|Suggest can be followed by a gerund or an appropriate that clause; the option going early is standard here.

Comprehension|A passage says, "The road closed because a bridge was damaged." What caused the closure?|Damage to the bridge|A new ticket price|A festival not mentioned|A shortage of bus drivers|Choose the cause explicitly stated in the passage. Do not add an unsupported explanation.

Comprehension|A passage calls a result "possible but unconfirmed". Which statement is supported?|The result is uncertain|The result is definitely proved|The result is impossible|The result has been independently verified|Possible but unconfirmed expresses uncertainty, not certainty or impossibility.

Comprehension|Which strategy best identifies a passage's main idea?|Find the central claim supported across the passage|Choose the longest word|Use only the final punctuation mark|Ignore examples and context entirely|A main idea summarizes the central message; supporting details should connect to it.
